title: NKCC1 coordinates SPAK–PP1 signalling to regulate KCC2 membrane stability and seizure susceptibility
title_zh: NKCC1 通过协调 SPAK–PP1 信号通路调节 KCC2 膜稳定性与癫痫易感性
abstract: Abstract Chloride homeostasis, and thereby the efficacy of chloride-permeable GABAA receptor signaling, depends on the dynamic balance between NKCC1 (Na+–K+–2Cl− cotransporter 1) and KCC2 (K+–Cl− cotransporter 2), which respectively mediate chloride influx and extrusion to tightly control intracellular chloride concentration ([Cl−]i). Here, we uncover an unexpected mechanism by which NKCC1 regulates KCC2 membrane stability and function. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments from mouse brain lysates revealed that KCC2 associates with NKCC1 and SPAK (STE20/SPS1-related proline-alanine-rich kinase), indicating that these proteins are within a common molecular interaction network. Furthermore, we show that NKCC1 and KCC2 form co-clusters in the plasma membrane of hippocampal neurons and that freely diffusing KCC2 molecules become trapped within NKCC1 membrane clusters. These observations suggest that NKCC1 coordinates SPAK- and PP1-dependent regulation of KCC2. Guided by molecular modeling, we designed peptides targeting specific interactions within this complex. Peptides that activate SPAK by engaging NKCC1’s PP1-binding motif decrease KCC2 surface expression and impair chloride extrusion, whereas a SPAK-inhibiting peptide that prevents SPAK recruitment to NKCC1, stabilizes KCC2 in membrane clusters, and enhances chloride extrusion. An optimized peptide analog suitable for in vivo use preserves KCC2 clustering under hyperexcitable conditions, reduces seizure frequency and severity in an acute pentylenetetrazol-induced (PTZ) seizure model, and suppresses ictal activity in chronically epileptic human tissue. Together, these findings identify NKCC1 as a key regulator of KCC2 membrane stability, reveal NKCC1-KCC2 coupling as a critical determinant of inhibitory signaling, and establish this complex as a potential therapeutic target for restoring chloride homeostasis in epilepsy and related neurological disorders.
abstract_zh: 摘要：氯离子稳态以及由此决定的可通氯 GABAA 受体信号的有效性，取决于 NKCC1（Na⁺–K⁺–2Cl⁻ 同步转运蛋白 1）与 KCC2（K⁺–Cl⁻ 同步转运蛋白 2）之间的动态平衡，后者分别介导氯离子内流与外流，以严格控制细胞内氯离子浓度（[Cl⁻]ᵢ）。本研究揭示了 NKCC1 调节 KCC2 膜稳定性与功能的意外机制。对小鼠脑组织裂解液进行共免疫沉淀实验显示，KCC2 与 NKCC1 及 SPAK（STE20/SPS1 相关富含脯氨酸-丙氨酸激酶）相互结合，表明这些蛋白位于同一分子互作网络中。进一步观察发现，NKCC1 与 KCC2 在海马神经元质膜上形成共聚集体，自由扩散的 KCC2 分子被困于 NKCC1 膜聚集体内。这些结果提示 NKCC1 协调 SPAK 与 PP1 对 KCC2 的调控。基于分子建模，我们设计了靶向该复合物特定相互作用的肽段。通过激活 NKCC1 的 PP1 结合基序来激活 SPAK 的肽段可降低 KCC2 表面表达并削弱氯离子外流；而抑制 SPAK 招募至 NKCC1 的肽段则能稳定 KCC2 在膜聚集体中，并增强氯离子外流。经过优化的肽类模拟物适用于体内使用，在高兴奋状态下保持 KCC2 聚集，降低急性 5-氯-2-丙基-2-硝基苯并噻嗪（PTZ）诱导的癫痫发作频率与严重程度，并抑制慢性癫痫人类组织中的发作活动。综上所述，这些发现确定了 NKCC1 作为 KCC2 膜稳定性的关键调节因子，揭示了 NKCC1–KCC2 结合是抑制性信号的关键决定因素，并将该复合物确立为恢复癫痫及相关神经疾病中氯离子稳态的潜在治疗靶点。
